record.paper_title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
record.original_question: In the scale-invariant regime for geometric curvature energies, what is the optimal regularity of finite-energy Lipschitz curves or submanifolds? For a higher-dimensional generalization of Möbius energy, how regular are finite-energy submanifolds? What are the optimal constants in Fenchel-type theorems that bound the energy needed to close a curve or a surface? And if a k-dimensional manifold immersed in R^n has finite scale-invariant tangent-point energy or finite scale-invariant integral Menger curvature, must its image automatically be embedded?

evidence.quote: The scale-invariant exponent for integral Menger curvature Mp(Σ) on two-dimensional surfaces Σ ⊂ R3 is p = 8, and we proved a Fenchel-type theorem [120, Theorem 1.2].

Open questions 2.2.10. What is the optimal regularity of finite energy Lipschitz curves or submanifolds for any of the geometric curvature energies in the scale-invariant case? How regular are submanifolds of finite energy for a suitable generalisation of the Möbius energy to higher dimensional objects? How much geometric curvature energy does one really need to close a curve or a surface, in other words what are the optimal constants in Fenchel-type theorems like Theorem 2.2.9? Is every k-dimensional manifold Mk immersed in Rn automatically embedded if its image has finite scale-invariant tangent-point energy E2k (see (2.1.10)), or finite scale-invariant integral Menger curvature Mk(k+2) (see (2.1.11))?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For an integer k ≥ 1 and n > k, let M be a k-dimensional smooth manifold and γ: M → ℝⁿ an immersion with image Σ = γ(M). Define the tangent-point radius r_tp(x,y) for distinct x,y ∈ Σ as the radius of the smallest ball through x and y that is tangent to the tangent plane T_xΣ at x. For exponents p > 0, the tangent-point energy is

  E_p(Σ) = ∫_Σ ∫_Σ (1/r_tp(x,y))^p dℋ^k(x) dℋ^k(y),

and the integral Menger curvature is

  M_p(Σ) = ∫_Σ ··· ∫_Σ K(x_0,…,x_{k+1})^p dℋ^k(x_0)···dℋ^k(x_{k+1}),

where K(x_0,…,x_{k+1}) is the inverse of the circumradius of the (k+2)-tuple. The scale-invariant exponents are p = 2k for E_p and p = k(k+2) for M_p. A higher-dimensional Möbius-type energy for k-submanifolds is defined analogously, with the appropriate scale-invariant exponent.

Problems. Consider the scale-invariant regime, i.e. p = 2k for the tangent-point energy E_{2k}, p = k(k+2) for the integral Menger curvature M_{k(k+2)}, and the analogous scale-invariant Möbius-type energy on k-submanifolds.

(a) Determine the optimal regularity (in the scale of Sobolev, Hölder, or Besov spaces) of an arbitrary Lipschitz curve (k = 1) or k-dimensional submanifold of ℝⁿ that has finite scale-invariant energy, for each of these energies.

(b) For the higher-dimensional generalization of the Möbius energy to k-dimensional submanifolds in ℝⁿ, determine the optimal regularity of finite-energy submanifolds.

(c) Determine the optimal (smallest) constant c_E in Fenchel-type lower bounds of the form
  E(Σ) ≥ c_E
for every closed (i.e. compact without boundary) k-submanifold Σ ⊂ ℝⁿ, where E ranges over the scale-invariant geometric curvature energies above.

(d) Let M be a k-dimensional smooth manifold and γ: M → ℝⁿ an immersion. Show, or find a counterexample to, the following statement: if γ(M) has finite scale-invariant tangent-point energy E_{2k}, or finite scale-invariant integral Menger curvature M_{k(k+2)}, then γ is automatically an embedding.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate sharp results are known in the supercritical (above scale-invariant) regime—e.g. finite tangent-point energy E_p with p > 2k yields C^{1,μ} regularity with optimal Hölder exponent μ = 1 − 2k/p, and embeddedness follows—but the scale-invariant cases p = 2k and p = k(k+2) remain delicate. Recent work (Blatt–Reiter–Vorderobermeier, 2021, on scale-invariant tangent-point energies for knots) addresses minimizers/critical points in the scale-invariant regime for curves but does not resolve optimal regularity of arbitrary finite-energy Lipschitz objects, optimal Fenchel-type constants, or the automatic-embeddedness question in full generality for k ≥ 1. Thus the cluster of questions appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Scale-invariant tangent-point energies for knots (arXiv:2104.10238)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimizers and critical points in ambient isotopy classes for scale-invariant tangent-point energies of closed curves; addresses convergence and regularity of critical embeddings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on the scale-invariant case for curves; broader optimal regularity, sharp Fenchel constants, and automatic-embeddedness in the scale-invariant regime are not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Regularity theory for tangent-point energies: the non-degenerate sub-critical case (arXiv:1208.3605)
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp C^{1,μ} regularity with μ = 1 − 2m/q for finite tangent-point energy with q > 2m (supercritical regime).
status_evidence.claim: Optimal regularity is established only above scale invariance; the scale-invariant exponent case is left open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions on optimal regularity in the scale-invariant case, Fenchel-type optimal constants, and automatic embeddedness for finite scale-invariant tangent-point energy or integral Menger curvature.
status_evidence.claim: These problems are explicitly posed as open.
